newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, March 1 Initial Claims from 310,000, March 1 4-Week Average from 310,000, Feb 22 Continued Claims from 2,377,000 and Feb 15 from 2,404,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 313,000 in the March 8 week.
The department said continued claims of 2,335,000 in the week ending March 1 was at the lowest level since May 7, 1990, when claims hit 2,317,000.
Labor said five states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended March 1, the latest period for which data are available.
They were Massachusetts, with 4,126; Texas, with 2,166; Michigan, with 2,119; Rhode Island, with 1,359; and Connecticut, with 1,173.

Massachusetts and Connecticut gave no reason for the drop in claims. Texas said it had fewer layoffs in the service industry, while Michigan reported fewer layoffs in various industries throughout the state. Rhode Island reported fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries and in manufacturing.
There were five states reporting increases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the March 1 week.
They were New York, with 8,320; Arkansas, with 1,694; Ohio, with 1,509; New Jersey, with 1,197; and Illinois, with 1,184.

New York linked its increase to the return to the five-day work week after a shorter reporting period the week before. It also reported layoffs in various industries. Arkansas had layoffs in the food and transportation equipment industries.
New Jersey and Illinois both reported layoffs in the trade and service industries and in manufacturing. Ohio had no comment.
